definitions.explanation: Describes fruit or crops that have not fully ripened.
Describes a person whose skills, knowledge, or character are not yet fully developed.

examples.japanese: {未熟|みじゅく}な{果実|かじつ}。
まだ{未熟|みじゅく}なトマトは{食|た}べない{方|ほう}がいい。
examples.english: It's better not to eat tomatoes that aren't ripe yet.

examples.japanese: この{品種|ひんしゅ}は{未熟|みじゅく}な{状態|じょうたい}で{収穫|しゅうかく}されることが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: This variety is often harvested while still unripe.

examples.japanese: まだまだ{未熟|みじゅく}です。
{未熟|みじゅく}な{医者|いしゃ}に{手術|しゅじゅつ}されたくない。
examples.english: I don't want to be operated on by an unskilled doctor.

examples.japanese: {技術|ぎじゅつ}が{未熟|みじゅく}なうちは{失敗|しっぱい}も{多|おお}いが、{経験|けいけん}を{積|つ}めば{上達|じょうたつ}する。
examples.english: While your skills are still undeveloped there will be many mistakes, but with experience you'll improve.

notes:
Composed of {未|み} (not yet) + {熟|じゅく} (ripe/mature). The word connects the literal sense of unripeness with the figurative sense of human immaturity. Sense 2 is far more common in everyday usage.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {未熟|みじゅく}な{技術|ぎじゅつ}: undeveloped skill
- {未熟|みじゅく}な{判断|はんだん}: immature judgment
- {未熟|みじゅく}な{者|もの}: inexperienced person
- まだまだ{未熟|みじゅく}: still very inexperienced (humble self-description)

USAGE:
When used about oneself, it functions as a humble expression acknowledging one's lack of skill. まだまだ{未熟|みじゅく}です is a common phrase used when receiving praise.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {未経験|みけいけん}: inexperienced — focuses on lack of experience rather than lack of skill development
- {若|わか}い: young — can imply inexperience but without the negative skill connotation
- {半人前|はんにんまえ}: half-baked, not yet fully trained — implies being halfway to competence
- {熟練|じゅくれん}: skilled, experienced — the opposite of {未熟|みじゅく}
